current_episode.title: Why Knoxville Is One of America's Fastest-Growing Markets

guest.bio_context: Justin Kazana is a third-generation commercial real estate professional with deep expertise in the Knoxville market. He holds both the SIOR and CCIM designations and specializes in tenant and landlord representation across office, industrial, and retail asset classes. Before transitioning to commercial real estate over two decades ago, he worked in television and radio sports broadcasting, including minor league baseball, Fox Sportsnet, and Comcast Sports. He played a key role in opening Cushman & Wakefield's Knoxville office in 2010 and led the migration to Avis & Young in 2015, where the Knoxville office has grown to 25 brokers managing nearly three million square feet.

pending_qa.q: Why did the Knoxville Avis & Young office migrate from Cushman & Wakefield in 2015?
pending_qa.r: The decision to migrate from Cushman & Wakefield to Avis & Young in 2015 was driven by Cushman's acquisition by DTZ. The Knoxville office wanted to maintain local ownership and favorable commission splits that work for a tertiary market like Knoxville, rather than being required to meet Cushman's national commission splits that would have caused them to lose brokers. About 84 people made the transition across the Knoxville, Nashville, and Memphis offices to Avis & Young.

pending_qa.q: How did Justin Kazana transition from sports broadcasting at Fox Sportsnet to commercial real estate in Knoxville?
pending_qa.r: Justin worked in television and radio sports broadcasting for nearly 10 years, including roles at Fox Sportsnet and Comcast Sports doing play-by-play for SEC football championships and Olympic sports. However, he decided to transition back to the family business around 2004 when he realized the broadcasting hours and travel schedule conflicted with raising a family, as sports do not take place nine to five Monday through Friday. He returned to Knoxville and worked with his father for six years in property management and development before opening the Cushman & Wakefield office.
